title: The total that ignores the first die
hook: You peek at the first of two dice. Does that tell you anything about the total?

knows: two dice have 36 equally likely outcomes
a chance as a share of equally likely cases
doesNotKnow: how to test whether two events affect each other
that events built from the same dice can still be independent

misconception: If two events involve the same dice they must influence each other, so seeing the first die must change the chance of a total of 7.
objective: The learner can explain that a total of 7 stays at 1/6 whatever the first die shows (one 7 in every row), so the two are independent, while a total of 8 moves from 5/36 to 1/6 or 0 and is not.
keyState: A first-die clue tried on total 7 (stays 1/6), then on total 8 (moves away from 5/36).

claims.text: A total of 7 has 6 of 36 outcomes (1/6), and given any first die it is still 1/6: every row holds exactly one 7.
claims.source: Enumeration (before(7), after(7, k) for k = 1..6 in src/demos/probability/sum-seven-ignores-first-die/model.ts).

claims.text: A total of 8 has 5 of 36 outcomes (13.9%); given a first die of 2 to 6 it becomes 1/6 (16.7%), and given a first die of 1 it is 0.
Two events are independent when knowing one leaves the chance of the other unchanged.
claims.source: Definition: P(A | B) = P(A), equivalently P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B); for total 7 and first die 3: 1/36 = 1/6 x 1/6.

recall.question: You draw a card from a full deck. Does learning it is a heart change the chance that it is an ace?
recall.why: 4 of 52 cards are aces (1 in 13), and 1 of the 13 hearts is an ace (1 in 13). The clue leaves the chance unchanged: suit and ace are independent.
